changes.text: 一群在美国读书的中国朋友，为“诗能不能用白话写”吵了一年多。1916年7月，湖上一场几乎翻船的风雨，和一位朋友用老字写成的纪事诗，又掀起一轮新的争吵。站在一边的是胡适，而他一向说自己是保守的人，认为语言文字是世界上最保守的东西，比宗教还保守，还说自己这一路是被「逼上梁山」的。这句成语说的是一个人为环境所迫，不得已而做出违反他本意的非常行为。

A group of Chinese friends studying in America argued for more than a year over whether poetry could be written in baihua, the everyday spoken language. In July 1916 a storm on a lake that nearly capsized their boat, and a friend's poem about it written in archaic words, set off a fresh round of quarrelling. On one side stood Hu Shi, who called himself a conservative: language and writing, he liked to say, are the most conservative things in the world, more conservative than religion. He also said he had been pushed down this road: bi shang Liangshan, driven to Liangshan, an idiom for someone forced by circumstances into extraordinary acts against his own intentions.

反对他的主要是两位朋友：一位是去哈佛升学、最坚定的反对者梅光迪，另一位是同在康乃尔、写诗嘲笑过他的任鸿隽。争的是白话能不能用来写文学。到1916年夏天，朋友们已承认白话可以写小说、演说，唯独不肯承认它能作诗，反对者已经退到只剩一处：诗。按胡适的说法，难处在于从来没有中国作家认真着实用白话作诗，他在中国诗词中能找到的白话诗只有一首，甚至只是一首中的几句。按他自己的说法，把他推向后来那个决定的，不是什么大事件，而是一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件。

His chief opponents were two friends: Mei Guangdi, bound for Harvard and his most determined opponent, and Ren Hongjun, also at Cornell, who had mocked him in verse. The quarrel was over whether the vernacular could serve literature. By the summer of 1916 his friends granted that it would do for fiction and speeches, but not for poetry. Poetry was the last fortress. The difficulty, as Hu saw it, was that no Chinese writer had ever seriously written poetry in the vernacular; in all of Chinese verse he could find only one such poem, perhaps only a few lines of one. In his own telling, what pushed him toward the decision that followed was no great event, but a small accident set off by a farewell poem.
更早还有一段引子。一位热心改革的书记，总在留学生每月的奖学金支票信封里夹寄小传单，其中一条是「废除汉字，改用字母！」。约在1915年（胡适说“我想是”），胡适回了一张很不客气的字条，叫他「最好闭起鸟嘴！」

There was an earlier prelude. A clerk keen on reform used to slip leaflets into the envelopes that carried the students' monthly scholarship checks; one slogan, in translation, was to abolish the Chinese characters and switch to an alphabet. Around 1915 (Hu said he thought it was then), Hu wrote back a rude little note telling the man, in translation, that he had better shut his beak.
字条寄出后他心中懊悔，觉得不该对一位和善又有心改革的人如此不礼貌。他还想到：假如这样的人不够资格谈这个问题，那么够资格的人实在更该认真研究。于是他和一位同学商定，在留学生会的年会上各写一篇论文讨论中国文字问题，他自己的题目是怎样使文言易于教授。

Once the note was sent he regretted it: the man was kind and sincere about reform, and the rudeness was uncalled for. Then a further thought: if men like him were not qualified to discuss the question, the qualified should do the work. So he agreed with a fellow student that each would write a paper on the problem of the Chinese script for the annual meeting of a Chinese students' association. Hu's topic was how to make the classical written language easier to teach.

争论是从一首送别诗开始的。胡适准备离开康乃尔时，梅光迪正要去哈佛升学。胡适写了首相当长的打油诗为他送行，里面塞进十一个外国人的名字。同在康乃尔的任鸿隽把这些名字连缀起来，作诗嘲笑他「文学今革命，作诗送胡生！」。胡适自认那首送行诗立意严肃：诗里鼓励朋友们留意今后中国文学的发展，并说致力于中国文学革命，贡献不下于征服自然，他叫它作「缩地戡天」。所以他不肯轻轻放过，在去纽约的火车上作了答诗，第一次写下“诗国革命”的念头：「诗国革命何自始？要须作诗如作文！」

It began with a farewell poem. When Hu was preparing to leave Cornell, Mei Guangdi was about to go on to Harvard. Hu sent him off with a doggerel poem, long by Chinese standards, stuffed with eleven foreign names. Ren Hongjun, also at Cornell, strung the names into a mock verse of his own, which in our translation runs: literature's revolution today, a poem to send off Hu. Hu would not let it pass. His send-off had been meant in earnest. It urged his friends to watch where Chinese literature went next, and it ranked a revolution in Chinese literature with conquering nature, which he called, in our translation, shrinking the earth and taming the heavens. So on the train to New York he wrote an answer, and in it first set down the idea of a revolution in the poetry world. His couplet, in our translation, asks where that revolution should begin, and answers that poetry must be written like prose.

转机出现在1916年二三月。他形成一个概括观念：整部中国文学史就是一部文学工具变迁史，一个工具替代另一个工具；同时也是一部活文学逐渐代替死文学的历史。工具一旦活力消失、逐渐僵化，就要换一个，在这种嬗递中接受一个活的工具，他称之为“文学革命”。三月，他写长信给在哈佛的梅光迪，说中古以后老的语言工具已不够用，变迁在唐代便已发生：散文体裁发生革命，逐渐发展出以白话表达的语录体，先为和尚们采用，后来宋代哲学家用它记录哲学讨论，老百姓又用它作歌曲、编戏剧、写短篇和长篇小说。他说用白话写的活文学，最明显的如元曲，是民众不知不觉中完成的文学革命的最高潮，中国文学之复苏实得力于白话戏曲和白话小说之兴起。出乎他意料，这套由历史分析得出的结论，竟被这位保守朋友欣然接受。需要补一句：他们当时以为传统长篇小说都是元代作品，胡适本人晚年更正说，《水浒》一流的故事流传几百年，到明代才写成定稿。

The turn came in February and March of 1916. Hu reached a general idea: the history of Chinese literature is a history of changing literary tools, one replacing another, and at the same time a history of living literature gradually displacing dead literature. When a tool loses its vitality and hardens it must be changed, and taking up a living tool in that succession is what he called literary revolution. In March he wrote a long letter to Mei, then at Harvard. After the medieval period, he wrote, the old language tool could no longer carry people's thoughts. The change had begun in the Tang, when prose style was revolutionized and a vernacular recorded-sayings style grew up. Monks took it up first, then Song philosophers used it for their discussions, and then ordinary people used it for songs, plays, stories and novels. Vernacular literature of that kind, Yuan drama most obviously, was, he said, the climax of a literary revolution the masses completed without knowing it; the revival of Chinese literature owed much to the rise of vernacular drama and fiction. To Hu's surprise, this conclusion drawn from historical analysis was gladly accepted by his conservative friend. One note: they then took the great traditional novels for Yuan works. Hu corrected himself in later years, saying that stories like Water Margin circulated for centuries before being written down in final form under the Ming.

两天之后，湖上出了桩险事。7月8日，任鸿隽、梅光迪等几位朋友在凯约嘉湖上划船，片云头上黑，忽然刮起风暴，雨落下来。他们急忙往岸边划，几乎把船弄翻，个个淋得狼狈不堪。对这批中国留学生来说，这也算件险事。任鸿隽随后写了一首四言古诗《泛湖即事》附在信里，请胡适批评。诗中用了《诗经》里“言”字一类的老字，而胡适此前恰好写过一篇《言字解》。他不喜欢这种陈腐文字与现代语言夹杂，回信说此诗不好，因为「文字殊不调和」，又有「三千年前之死语」之说。任鸿隽不服，愤愤不平。更有意思的是梅光迪路见不平，写来一封十分激动的信反击。梅当时正受他那位保守派文学批评老师的影响，对胡适的一切激进主张都反对到底。他认为语言必须经过第一流的诗人加以锻炼，才能成为诗的语言；文学的文字，尤其是诗的文字，一定要由第一流的诗人和美术家加以美化，才能成为诗之文字。他据此对胡适的观念大加挞伐。

Two days later came a close call on Cayuga Lake. On July 8 Ren Hongjun, Mei Guangdi and several other friends were rowing on the lake when a black cloud gathered overhead, a storm broke and the rain fell. Pulling for shore in a hurry they nearly capsized, and all came away soaked and dishevelled. For that band of Chinese students it was a real adventure, and Ren wrote it up in Fanhu jishi (Boating on the Lake), an old four-character-style poem he mailed to Hu for criticism. It used archaic words such as the particle yan, of the kind found in the Book of Songs. Hu had earlier written an essay on that very word, and he disliked dead diction mixed with modern language. He wrote back that the poem was bad because its wording was thoroughly incongruous, and he spoke of dead language of three thousand years ago (both paraphrased from the Chinese). Ren was indignant. More interesting was the letter that followed: Mei, riding to the rescue in high dudgeon. Mei was under the influence of his conservative teacher, a literary critic, and he opposed all of Hu's radicalism to the end. Language becomes poetic, he held, only after first-rate poets refine it, and the language of literature, poetry above all, must be beautified by first-rate poets and artists before it counts as poetic diction. On that ground he lashed Hu's ideas.

胡适的回应是一首约一百句的滑稽打油诗，是他生平写的最长的一首。开头描写老梅大发脾气，再举许多例子开玩笑地驳“文字哪有死活”，并顺着对方的论点反将一军：文字须经诗人长期锻炼，这正是他想做的事，当代的诗人作家正该把这些俗语俗字锻炼起来，提高它们的地位，把它们提到诗歌文学里来。两位朋友读了大发雷霆，复信取笑他企图作白话诗。但胡适在信里发现两人有个共同的论调：白话的生动可以用在评话、故事、长篇小说等写作上，就是不能用在诗里。梅光迪排除得更多：在小说和民歌里白话可以用，但在高级散文里，肯定的是在诗里面，白话千万用不得。任鸿隽说得最干脆：「白话自有白话用处（如作小说、演说等），然不能用之于诗！」按胡适的归纳，朋友们在其他方面都已让步，只剩诗这一处还在争。

Hu answered with a comic doggerel poem of about a hundred lines, the longest he ever wrote. It opened with Old Mei in a towering rage, piled up examples to mock the theory that words have no life or death, and turned Mei's own argument against him: if words must be forged by poets over long practice, that is exactly what he wanted. Contemporary poets and writers should take these vulgar, colloquial words, temper them, raise their standing and bring them into poetry. The burlesque threw both friends into a fury, and both wrote back to mock his attempt at vernacular verse. Yet Hu found a common line in their letters: the liveliness of the vernacular could serve storytelling, tales and novels, but not poetry. Mei excluded more: the vernacular was usable in fiction and folk songs, but in high prose, and certainly in poetry, it must never be used. Ren was bluntest; his letter said, in translation, that the vernacular has its own uses, such as novels and speeches, but cannot be used for poetry. As Hu summed it up, his friends had given way everywhere else; only poetry was still in dispute.

In November 1916 he shaped more than a year of argument into an article with eight very moderate suggestions. Even the title was modest: he dropped "literary revolution," a phrase that had come up often in his own poems and letters and in his friends' letters to him, sometimes in jest and sometimes in earnest. This was the first time the conclusions would be sent home to China for publication. By his own later account, it was in view of the undoubted resistance of the older conservatives that he kept the wording gentle: reform, not revolution; a humble opinion, not dogma. He made three copies. One went to the Chinese Students' Quarterly he edited in America, then printed by the Commercial Press. Another went to New Youth, which Chen Duxiu, from 1916 dean of arts at National Peking University, had been editing for several years.

1917年一月，文章在《新青年》刊出，文化界反应很大。北大有两位教授重视它。一位是陈独秀本人，本是死硬派的革命人物，随后写《文学革命论》响应，公开支持文学革命，并说首举义旗的是朋友胡适，自己高张大旗作声援。另一位是研究古典音韵学的教授，也是古文大家，他没有写文章，却写去小批评大捧场的长信，也在《新青年》发表，声势为之一振。胡适在康乃尔的同学、当年与他分写论文的赵元任，则常说胡适的白话诗文“不够白”，不是一般人常用的真正语体。胡适承认了，还打了个比方：像裹了四十年或者二十年小脚的女人，纵使把小脚放大，终究恢复不了天足。

It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. One was Chen Duxiu himself, an unbending revolutionary. He answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he himself was raising the banner high in his friend's support. The other, a professor of classical phonology and a master of ancient prose, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters of small criticisms and great praise, also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren, Hu's fellow student at Cornell and his partner in the earlier pair of papers, often said, in our translation, that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were not vernacular enough, not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it. He compared himself to a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years: however much she loosened the bindings, she would never recover natural feet.

胡适自己对来龙去脉的解释是反对单因论。他开玩笑说，历史上的意外事件往往比“单因”（经济、色欲、上帝之类）更重要：正因为这些单因对所有事件皆可解释，它们也就不可解释任何事件。就他这段经历而言，他明确把送别诗称作「意外的小事」，并说「一连串的小意外事件，逐渐地强迫我采取了这个立场」。他也把湖上险事称作「小小的意外事件」，说它「引起了连锁性的反应」。本文把那张传单也放进这一串，这是本文的归并。把一连串小意外看作推力，是他本人的史观，不是本文的结论。

Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. He used to joke that accidents often matter more than any monistic cause, such as economics, lust or God: those single causes explain everything that has ever happened, and precisely because they explain everything, they explain nothing. In this episode he explicitly called the farewell poem a small accident, and said that a chain of small accidents had gradually forced him into his position. Hu himself also called the Cayuga Lake incident a small accident that set off a chain reaction. Adding the leaflet to that chain is this article's own grouping. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.

结局也可以交代一笔。胡适自述，运动约四年就在学校教育上基本成功：1920年北京政府教育部通令，国民小学一、二年级教材一律改用白话，旧教材分期废除。他说这场斗争“至少获得了部分的胜利”，其中重要的部分是以白话为教育工具。他同时说，1919年的学生运动把文化运动变成了政治运动，对文艺复兴运动是一种“干扰”，虽则对传播白话文功不可没。但他也说自己「还是感觉到不满意」：四十年来白话文始终没有成为完全的教育工具和文学工具。他把主要原因归于执政者的保守，以及文白夹杂的教科书。这是他本人的判断。

The outcome can be set down too. By Hu's account, in only about four years the effort to replace the classical language with the vernacular in the schools had all but succeeded: in 1920 the Ministry of Education of the Beijing government ordered that all first- and second-year textbooks in the national primary schools be written entirely in the vernacular, with the old textbooks abolished in stages. He said the struggle had won at least a partial victory, the important part being the vernacular as the instrument of education. He also said the student movement of 1919 had been an interruption to the Renaissance movement, turning a cultural movement into a political one, though it did much to spread the vernacular. Yet he said he still felt dissatisfied: in forty years the vernacular had never become a complete instrument of education and literature. He blamed this chiefly on the conservatism of those in power and on textbooks that mixed the classical and the vernacular. This is his own judgment.
他为何用“改良”不用“革命”，是本人事后的解释。唐德刚的说法则是译注者的评论：他认为“文言是半死的文字”这句口号当年有摧枯拉朽的功能，但真实性值得重新商榷；他又认为白话文是百分之百成功，白话诗则未必，至少还未脱离“尝试”阶段。

Why he used reform rather than revolution is his own retrospective explanation. Tang Degang's remarks are the annotator's commentary: he thought the slogan that the classical language is a half-dead form of writing had a devastating force in its day, but that its truth is worth debating again; and he judged vernacular prose a hundred per cent successful, while vernacular poetry was not necessarily so, and at least had not yet left the experimental stage.
唐德刚也记下，反对胡适的人觉得他居功太多；1956年胡适在哈佛大学以这一论调讲演时，后来为他作传的格里德简直嗤之以鼻。
Tang also records that Hu's opponents felt he claimed too much credit; when Hu gave this account in a 1956 lecture at Harvard, Jerome B. Grieder, later his biographer, simply scoffed at it.
本文只有胡适晚年口述一种来源，且经节译、手订与回译。梅光迪、任鸿隽的言行均为胡适转述，胡适对动机的说明是事后自述。唐德刚注释中的评价与推论属评论；注中所记之事（如1956年胡适在哈佛讲演时格里德的反应）是唐德刚的记述，本文未另行核验。凡标为 interpretation 的段落是作者推断，标为 modern 的段落是为今日读者虚构的场景。

This piece rests on a single source: Hu Shi's oral memoir in later life, itself abridged, revised in his own hand and translated back. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and deeds reach us only through Hu's retelling, and Hu's explanations of motive are retrospective. Tang Degang's evaluations and inferences are commentary; the events he records (such as Grieder's reaction to Hu's 1956 Harvard lecture) are his testimony, not checked here. Paragraphs marked interpretation are the author's inferences, and paragraphs marked modern are scenarios invented for readers today.

dispositions.rationale: hook.1 中英同步补写难处：从来没有中国作家认真用白话作诗，可找到的白话诗只有一首、甚至几句。没有采用建议稿中“手里没有一首现成的例子”的写法，因为证据说他能找到一首，照证据收窄。ev 加入 HS-E20。

我只能找到一首——甚或一首中的几句——是用白话文写的

dispositions.rationale: context.0 压缩为两句：删去庚款、清华学生监督处、钟文鳌姓名出身和另两条传单，只留一位热心改革的书记夹寄主张废除汉字的传单，以及胡适的回条。保留约1915年和“我想是”的限定。“半死的语言”仍在 context.2。

dispositions.rationale: 按读者优先要求重排，所有改动只删减或改写已有内容。(1) 开头改为朋友间一年多的争吵和湖上风雨引出的新争吵；hook.1 交代反对者、争点和难处，《尝试集》的决定留到 story.7 揭晓。(2) 主线人物固定为胡适、梅光迪、任鸿隽、陈独秀，首次出现时各用一句话说明身份。钟文鳌、白璧德、陈衡哲、杨铨、唐钺、钱玄同和外国人名改为泛称或删去；赵元任只在 story.9 理解必需处出现。(3) 传单与论文压缩为短段。(4) 删去绮色佳、麻州剑桥等地名。(5) limits.1 删去日期罗列。(6) 局限部分删去元明之辨与反事实补白，只保留来源性质、转述、事后解释和唐德刚评论的性质；因规则不得删段，仍分为三段短文字。(7) 结尾 today 两段已围绕可公开检验的试验和措辞取舍，未改。保留了已核实的限定：“我想是”、湖上事件的归属、胡适的“不满意”、唐德刚评论的性质。
